ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a heating curve, the vertical axis is labeled Temperature (°C), and the horizontal axis is labeled Energy Absorbed (kJ/kg). The curve first rises at a low temperature, then has a horizontal section at about 0°C, with W labeled nearby; next there is an upward-sloping line segment, labeled X; after reaching 100°C, a very long horizontal plateau appears, labeled Y; finally at the right end it rises upward again, with Z labeled nearby. Reasoning: The cooling effect of sweating comes from sweat absorbing heat when it evaporates from a liquid state into a gaseous state. When a phase change absorbs latent heat, the temperature remains unchanged, so on a heating curve it appears as a horizontal plateau. In the figure, the long horizontal plateau that represents liquid changing into gas is at 100°C, labeled Y. Therefore, what represents the cooling effect of sweating is Y.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it is a heating curve with temperature on the vertical axis and energy absorbed on the horizontal axis, with labels W, X, Y, and Z. Locate the segment representing evaporation: the cooling effect of sweating is due to sweat changing from liquid to vapor and absorbing latent heat, which appears as a constant-temperature plateau. On the graph, the long horizontal plateau at 100°C is labeled Y. Therefore the labeled part representing the cooling effect of sweating is Y.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一条加热曲线，纵轴标为 Temperature (°C)，横轴标为 Energy Absorbed (kJ/kg)。曲线先在低温处上升，然后在约 0°C 处有一段水平段，附近标有 W；接着有一段向上倾斜的线段，标有 X；到达 100°C 后出现一段很长的水平平台，标有 Y；最后在右端又向上升，附近标有 Z。推理：出汗的冷却作用来自汗液由液态蒸发为气态时吸收热量。相变吸收潜热时温度保持不变，因此在加热曲线上表现为水平平台。图中表示液体变为气体的长水平平台在 100°C 处，标记为 Y。因此代表出汗冷却作用的是 Y。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct heat-transfer interpretation of the heating curve: identify sweating with evaporation/latent heat and match that to the constant-temperature vaporization plateau on the graph. It is the natural single route for this question.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the graph as temperature versus energy absorbed. Note the labeled sections: W is a low-temperature plateau near 0°C, X is a sloped warming section up to 100°C, Y is the long horizontal section at 100°C, and Z is after the 100°C plateau at the far right.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question wording to focus specifically on the 'cooling effect of sweating,' not simply any warming region of the graph.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Sweating cools because liquid sweat evaporates from the skin; evaporation absorbs latent heat while temperature remains constant during a liquid-to-gas phase change. On a heating curve, this is shown by the horizontal plateau at the boiling/evaporation stage.
